clue.text: Horrible person, intellectual of a certain hue?

parts.note: a pig is a nasty, greedy person
mental means of the intellect

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a brainy person with an odd skin colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: pigmental means relating to pigment, so concerned with colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment is the substance giving colour, so pigmental loosely describes something to do with a particular colouring.

clue.text: Maiden rushed up to meet the first person in embrace

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden
ran, turned upwards
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A young woman runs up to greet the speaker with a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Inarm is a poetic verb meaning to clasp in one's arms.

clue.text: Highland assistant that is buried under wooded glen

indicators.note: in a down clue lying under something means coming after it

parts.note: a gill is a wooded ravine
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Highland helper lies buried beneath a forested valley.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie works for anglers or deer-stalkers on Scottish estates.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Highland attendant who helps sportsmen when fishing or hunting.

clue.text: African islander, once a prisoner in crushed condition

indicators.note: in places the prisoner letters within the other word

parts.note: mash is a pulpy, crushed state
lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A man from an African island was once jailed and left in a terrible state.
explanation.walkthrough: Malagash is an obsolete form of Malagasy, a native of Madagascar, hence 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a Malagasy, someone from the island of Madagascar off Africa's east coast.

clue.text: Indonesian den, one with nothing inside

indicators.note: inside means these letters go within the den word

parts.note: a nest, like a den, is a cosy lair or retreat
I is the Roman numeral one
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lair in Indonesia, a solitary one with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesiot is a Chambers word for an islander, specifically an inhabitant of the Indonesian archipelago.

clue.text: Sailors coming to American city where saint was born

parts.note: tars are sailors
US is the United States, so American

explanation.surface: Seamen arrive at a US town that was a saint's birthplace.
explanation.walkthrough: The saint is Paul, known as Saul of Tarsus before his conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarsus, in modern Turkey, was the birthplace of the apostle Paul.

clue.text: Helps when chance has to be seized

indicators.note: something seized is held in the grip of something else, so it goes inside

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a bet is a chance taken on an outcome

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand whenever an opportunity must be grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Like colourful festival, free for all

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and can move

parts.note: the letters of for all rearranged

explanation.surface: A bright carnival open to everyone at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Floral means of or decked with flowers, as a flower festival is.

clue.text: Mountain sheep loves to look down on valley and lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the part that looks down from above is placed first

parts.note: love is zero, O, here twice
a ria is a drowned river valley
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A wild sheep enjoys gazing from the heights over a valley and lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The oorial, or urial, is a wild sheep of the mountains of central Asia.

clue.text: Philanderer more prudent going round Arab land

indicators.note: going round something encircles it

parts.note: wiser means more sensible
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A sensible flirt travels around an Arab country.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser chases many women, as a philanderer does.

clue.text: A Parisian, I had to be member of a church

parts.note: un is French for a
taken as written
to have a meal is to eat, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: A Parisian speaker explains how they came to join a congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uniate belongs to an Eastern church in communion with Rome while keeping its own rites.

clue.text: Indian animal that's awful crossing a lake

indicators.note: crossing means the jeer word spans the other letters, holding them

parts.note: boo is the jeer that says that's awful
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A beast from India that is awful at getting across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Baloo is a Hindi word for a bear, the source of the bear's name in The Jungle Book.
explanation.definitionFit: A baloo is a bear in India, the Hindi name for the animal.

clue.text: Phone America for something to help broken bones

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A patient rings the States hoping for a cure for fractures.
explanation.definitionFit: A callus is the hard tissue that forms around a fracture and knits the broken bone together.

clue.text: Class with Scripture etc making one behave better

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school subject covering Scripture and the like
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school claims its Bible lessons improve pupils' conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, religious education, is the British school subject; form is the British word for a school year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform is to mend one's ways and start acting more properly than before.

clue.text: Corrupt celebrity in ill setting

indicators.note: a setting surrounds what is placed in it, as a mount holds a jewel

parts.note: ill as an adverb means badly
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A crooked famous figure is shown in a poor light.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastardly means debased or spurious, in the old sense of corrupted.

clue.text: Plant with bacterial disease — leaf's beginning to wither

indicators.note: to wither is to shrivel away, so the leaf's first letter dies off from the disease

parts.note: listeria is a bacterium, and the name is used for the illness it causes

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word leaf's

explanation.surface: A gardener's diagnosis: a plant has a bacterial infection, and its leaves start to shrivel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but supplies the opening W. The leaf's first letter is what withers away from the disease's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing shrub with hanging clusters of lilac flowers, so it is a garden plant.

clue.text: A short time entertaining one good chum abroad

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them in, so the inner letters go inside

parts.note: mo is short for moment
I is the Roman numeral one
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone briefly hosts a good friend from overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, so it is a pal as said in a foreign country.

clue.text: Strawberry about to be munched — the fellow's to eat it

indicators.note: to eat it means the possessive word takes the munched letters inside it

parts.note: his is the possessive of 'the fellow', so 'the fellow's' gives these letters

indicators.note: munched suggests chewing up, so the letters of 'about' are mashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man is about to bite into a strawberry he insists on eating himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be munched' rearranges ABOUT to AUTBO, which HIS takes inside, 'to eat it'. 'about' looks like a container signal but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hautbois, or hautboy, is an old name for a European wild strawberry with a musky flavour.

clue.text: Cent in terrible state, coin no longer usable

indicators.note: in means the cent letter goes inside the rearranged letters
terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters of 'state' are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A single cent in an awful condition is a coin you can no longer spend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STATE to SEATT, and C goes 'in' after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceatt was a small silver coin of Anglo-Saxon England, long out of circulation, hence no longer usable.

clue.text: Fabric is brought round to be displayed outside room

indicators.note: to be displayed outside means the turned letters go around the room word
brought round means the two letters of 'is' are turned the other way

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A fabric is carried round so it can be shown off outside a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round' turns IS into SI, which is 'to be displayed outside' HALL, the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Shalli, or challis, is a soft lightweight woven fabric of wool or cotton, often printed.

clue.text: Around home let's spread cheap decoration

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the home word
spread suggests the letters of 'let's' are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: Someone suggests draping cheap decorations all over the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges LET'S to TSEL, which goes 'Around' IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittering metallic strips used as decoration, a byword for showy but cheap ornament.

clue.text: Ignore little old cutie getting sozzled

indicators.note: someone sozzled is drunk and reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: O is the short form of old
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pay no attention to the old sweetheart who is getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone out is to freeze them out, deliberately snubbing them.

clue.text: Non-flying bird needs help — one taken outside to go up

indicators.note: something taken outside goes round the other piece
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: un is a dialect word for one, as in 'a good un'
to lend a hand is to help

explanation.surface: A flightless bird requires assistance from someone to get airborne.
explanation.definitionFit: Nhandu is another name for the rhea, the large flightless bird of South America.

clue.text: What one is looking for in new role is to kill time

indicators.note: in means the seeker word goes inside the rearranged letters
new suggests the letters of 'role' are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange
in hide-and-seek the seeker is 'it', the one doing the looking for others

explanation.surface: An actor in a new part admits they are just passing the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ROLE to LOER, with IT going 'in' after LO. IT is the seeker in the children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, and killing time is passing it aimlessly.

clue.text: Prostitutes having game start to linger repeatedly in back street

indicators.note: in here means the game and letters are placed inside the street abbreviation
back means the street abbreviation is turned round, read from the end
repeatedly says the letter from linger is written a second time

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the usual crossword game

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of linger

explanation.surface: Sex workers loiter again and again in a back alley, playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles the first letter of 'linger', and the street abbreviation, turned by 'back', wraps the game plus those two letters. 'having' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Trull is an archaic word for a prostitute or a loose woman, a Mephisto-style Chambers entry.

clue.text: Muscular youngster (old-fashioned type) has cut in

indicators.note: the word for cut is put in, so it sits inside the youngster

parts.note: a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s youth in Edwardian-style dress
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A retro-styled lad has had his hair trimmed and looks brawny.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a British youth fashion of the 1950s, often shortened to Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Thews are muscles or sinews, so thewed means well-muscled.

clue.text: Early woman, evil ultimately — I left husband, it is gathered

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: something gathered in is drawn inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: the last letter of evil
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A woman of old confesses that, being wicked, she walked out on her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilith fits the surface well: in legend she left Adam, her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish legend Lilith was Adam's first wife, created before Eve.

clue.text: Good material that adds a certain gloss

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, as glacé is an adjective

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
lace is a fabric

explanation.surface: Fine fabric that gives a shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacé describes a glazed, glossy finish, as on glacé kid leather or glacé icing.

clue.text: Sends back a wee amount

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the opposite way, so read it backwards

parts.note: to emit is to send out

explanation.surface: Someone returns only a tiny portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' hints at the Scots origin: stime is a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a stime is a glimmer or the smallest trace of something.

clue.text: African with long hair hugging duke

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap around, so the outer word encloses the other

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: An African with flowing locks embraces a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mande are a West African people, and the name covers their languages too.

clue.text: True stories coming from couples once more

parts.note: real means genuine or true
stories can mean fibs

explanation.surface: Genuine accounts are said to come from pairs who reunited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True stories' reads as a phrase but splits into two opposites; the answer is RE-ALLIES, not related to really.
explanation.definitionFit: To really is to ally again, so it joins two parties together a second time.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing to be stupid as before, having adopted new name

indicators.note: having adopted means taking the two letters into its middle

parts.note: doat is an old spelling of dote, to be silly or feeble-minded, so 'as before' marks the archaic form

explanation.surface: An idle wastrel behaves foolishly as he always did, after taking on a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' signals an archaic spelling of dote, the old word for being feeble-minded; the two N abbreviations go into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Donnat (or donnot) is a Scottish and dialect word for a worthless idler, a ne'er-do-well listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Distinct political group full of love repeatedly sweet-talking

indicators.note: full of means the group's word holds the love letters inside it

parts.note: a wing is a faction within a party, as in the left wing

indicators.note: repeatedly says the love letter appears twice in a row

parts.note: O is love, the zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A political faction, brimming with affection, keeps flattering people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles O, and 'full of' puts OO inside WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooing is courting someone with flattery and charm, which is what sweet-talking means.

clue.text: Playful lord in court in charge

parts.note: m'lud is how a barrister addresses a judge in a British court
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A frivolous judge presides over his court.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludic, from Latin ludus a game, means showing spontaneous, playful behaviour.

clue.text: Initial earnings with a debit to be arranged

indicators.note: to be arranged means the letters of 'a debit' are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An accountant notes early income alongside a debit still to be sorted out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be arranged' reorders the six letters of A DEBIT. 'Initial earnings' is a cryptic definition: the answer is a kind of earnings named by its initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: EBITDA stands for Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation, a measure of profit written as initials.

clue.text: Transvestites in red dancing in parties

indicators.note: one thing placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: a bash is a party

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a new order

parts.note: the letters of red rearranged

explanation.surface: Cross-dressers in red are dancing at parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Berdache is a term for Native American people who took on the dress and roles of the other sex.
